description: Return information about installed pip packages.

parameters.name: clients
parameters.description: A list of the pip executables that are used to get the packages. They can be supplied with the full path or just the executable name, for example pip3.7. Default: ["pip"]

examples:
- name: Just get the list from default pip
  community.general.pip_package_info:

- name: Get the facts for default pip, pip2 and pip3.6
  community.general.pip_package_info:
    clients: ['pip', 'pip2', 'pip3.6']

- name: Get from specific paths (virtualenvs?)
  community.general.pip_package_info:
    clients: '/home/me/projec42/python/pip3.5'

return_values.name: packages
return_values.description: A dictionary of installed package data. Returned: always

return_values.name: python
return_values.description: A dictionary with each pip client which then contains a list of dicts with python package information. Returned: always Sample: {"packages": {"pip": {"Babel": [{"name": "Babel", "source": "pip", "version": "2.6.0"}], "Flask": [{"name": "Flask", "source": "pip", "version": "1.0.2"}], "Flask-SQLAlchemy": [{"name": "Flask-SQLAlchemy", "source": "pip", "version": "2.3.2"}], "Jinja2": [{"name": "Jinja2", "source": "pip", "version": "2.10"}]}}}
